changes.summary: Separate review, edit, capture, apply and publication authority; correct hook semantics; preserve targeted capture, template and age expertise.

review.disposition: retain with authority corrections; candidate only

execution.alternatives: bounded independent inspection; worktrees do not isolate live HOME

limitations: No live harness or wrapper workflow execution.
No discovered license file; promotion and distribution remain human decisions.
Pack membership and implicit apply policy are recommendations, not accepted settings.

questions.question: Should source edits imply apply authority?
questions.rationale: Apply may trigger hooks and deploy unrelated pending changes.
questions.recommendation: Keep source edit and live apply separately authorized.

validation: Static walkthroughs of review-only, candidate-only, template edit, live capture and dirty-tree publication; inspected wrapper capture and git add -A behavior.

changes.summary: Replace false atomic claim guarantees, direct API fallback, hardcoded main/focus and artifact-only completion with scoped dispatcher claims, base validation, evidence and explicit review state.

review.disposition: retain explicit orchestration with corrected coordination

execution.alternatives: sequential in-session implementation; authorized Herdr topology for visibility
execution.recommended: single in-session dispatcher with bounded independent workers and isolated worktrees for concurrent code writes

review.invocation: explicit; retained disable-model-invocation requires provider verification
limitations: No live agent, worktree, build or ticket workflow executed by candidate.
Provider invocation metadata and current Herdr CLI must be verified before promotion.
No discovered license; external dispatchers can still race.

questions.question: Should one dispatcher own all claims and tracker updates?
questions.rationale: Shared self-assignment is not an atomic lock and hides child races.
questions.recommendation: Yes; workers return evidence rather than mutating shared ticket state.

questions.question: Does a sweep request alone authorize new Herdr topology?
questions.rationale: Visibility and write isolation differ, and new workspaces consume shared resources.
questions.recommendation: Confirm topology separately unless already specified; allow sequential execution.

validation: Static scenarios for shared identities, missing code prerequisites, untracked diffs, review-state dependencies, empty frontier, failed capacity and interruption.

changes.summary: Preserve design-tree frontier and human decisions; bound large rounds, make fact delegation optional and distinguish blocked or deferred branches from completion.

review.disposition: retain dependency-aware interview; comparison with related skills pending

execution.alternatives: bounded read-only fact lookup; no Herdr/worktree for the interview

review.invocation: task-triggered by a requested grilling or stress-test interview
limitations: Related grilling variants remain unreviewed; no retirement approved.
No discovered license; distribution and pack recommendation require human review.

questions.question: Preserve whole-frontier rounds or cap large rounds?
questions.rationale: Maintains decision coverage without overwhelming the interviewee.
questions.recommendation: Use the whole frontier for small sets; visibly split large independent sets.

validation: Static walkthroughs of dependency waits, large frontiers, unavailable facts, user pauses and confirmation without implementation authority; agent metadata retained after full read.

changes.summary: Correct non-atomic claims across entrypoint and references; preserve CLI mechanics, add failed-loader guard, project-only scope, lowest-number selection and acceptance-aware transitions.

review.disposition: retain shared tracker mechanics with coordinated claims

execution.alternatives: bounded read-only issue/source inspection; worktrees do not isolate Linear

review.invocation: task-triggered or reached by a composing tracker workflow
limitations: No atomic tracker exclusion is available; external dispatchers may race.
Credential snippet is Bash and supports only the managed single-line format.
No live provider metadata evaluation or discovered license; promotion not authorized.

questions.question: Make one dispatcher the default for shared-account claims?
questions.rationale: Shared self-assignment and read-after-write do not prove exclusive ownership.
questions.recommendation: Yes, with worker identity and exclusive file scope recorded.

validation: Full-tree static review and walkthroughs of shared identity, native blockers, explicit task destination, loader failure, partial writes and acceptance-aware resolution.
Driver observed CLI 2.5.0 help and HJ-729 read-only issue/relations; synthetic loader evidence is recorded in batch validation.

changes.summary: Preserve Go windows and override mechanics; separate read from refresh, verify workspace and freshness, distinguish input percentages/output fractions and recorded payload from panel success.

review.disposition: retain provider-local quota workflow with honest freshness and write boundaries

execution.alternatives: user-provided dashboard readings when browser access is absent; no delegated credentials or Herdr

review.invocation: task-triggered for Go quota or stale Go monitor figures only
limitations: No authenticated dashboard, scraper, override or monitor execution.
Current quota API availability and collector lifetime/fallback are not established by this candidate.
No discovered license; provider-local distribution remains a proposed policy.

questions.question: Should a usage question implicitly refresh the monitor?
questions.rationale: Scraper invokes an override and refresh; successful write does not prove display success.
questions.recommendation: No; observation by default, explicit refresh authority for writers.

validation: Read complete scraper and override source; static cases for stale snapshots, fixed workspace identity, payload failures, absent resets, percentage units and suppressed panel refresh errors.

changes.summary: Preserve scorecard, measurable roadmap and traceability expertise; remove invocation-implied policy writes and mandatory parallelism; reconcile read-only proposals and define evidence-based completion.

review.disposition: retain evidence-backed critic/planner roles with explicit writing authority

execution.alternatives: bounded critic/planner delegation for substantial independent work, one guidance writer; no default Herdr
execution.recommended: two in-session analytical passes for small inputs

review.invocation: task-triggered for project assessment and execution-plan requests
limitations: Local distribution mismatch remains integration work; no links or manifests changed.
No discovered license; write-authority and pack recommendations await human review.

questions.question: Should explicit invocation alone permit AGENTS.md and ROADMAP.md writes?
questions.rationale: Writable filesystem and skill invocation do not imply authority to change agent policy.
questions.recommendation: Require a request to create or update those files.

questions.question: Require two agents for every assessment?
questions.rationale: Small inputs can be assessed directly without losing critic/planner separation.
questions.recommendation: Retain two analytical roles, delegate only when scale and capacity justify it.

validation: Static walkthroughs of read-only planning, named-file writing, one-writer delegation, unknown metrics and findings-to-roadmap reconciliation; all provider metadata read and retained.
